dish: Danryū cask-aged awamori and Shurei kūsu (aged awamori) tasting
n: Kamimura Distillery Kūsu-gura (神村酒造 古酒蔵)
w: Awamori distillery founded in 1882 (originally in Naha's Shikina/Hantagawa), maker of Danryū — the 1968 cask-aged awamori credited with reviving post-war demand — and Shurei. Free ~40-minute tours (20 min distillery, 20 min tasting) by reservation, plus a direct shop and kūsu storage service.

dish: Hone-jiru (pork-backbone soup) and hone-soba with bone-in sōki
w: Local shokudō by Chatan's Mihama known for hone-jiru — pork backbones and tofu simmered in a kombu broth and eaten by hand — and hone-soba heaped with bone-in sōki; both often sell out early.

dish: Shima-soba with three mismatched noodle types
n: Sanchōme no Shima Soba-ya, Ginowan (3丁目の島そば屋)
address: 3-10-1 Kakazu, Ginowan, Okinawa, Japan (White Papillon Sato 101)
w: Newer Ginowan soba shop picked among the eight best soba shops of central Okinawa in Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle lovers; Okinawa TV's Okitive praised its noodles, soup and toppings, notably the uneven mix of three noodle cuts.

dish: Tacos with shells fried to order, and the Tacos-ya Plate (tacos, taco rice, onion rings, fries)
n: Tacos-ya Chatan (タコス屋 北谷店)
address: 1-5 Miyagi, Chatan, Okinawa, Japan (near the Sunabe Seawall)
w: Small taco shop on a backstreet near the Sunabe Seawall that has fed locals and visitors for about 35 years; it still fries its house-made shells to order for a chewy-crisp texture, and its Tacos-ya Plate piles tacos, taco rice, onion rings and fries on one plate.
